alex: Heads-up — after last night's attn-fusion kernel rollout + mixed-precision quant profile, we see a drop in seeded-context cache hit-rate for a subset of production routes, ~12% -> ~4%. Noticed during spike window around 02:10 UTC.

maria: Ugh. Any obvious error logs? e.g., key canonicalization or hash changes?

raj: Looking at the metrics: pfx_cache.hit_rate per route shows the drop only for routes with long prompt prefixes (avg 220 tokens). Shorter prompts unaffected.

alex: Attn-fusion changed attention tiling and we landed a small opt that pads sequence to 64 multiple; suspect padding-order impacts context hash. Also quant profile switched to q4_mixed on that host pool.

sophia: Can you paste the cache lookup log for a failing request? I want to see the key string.

alex: Sure — sample from /var/log/redwood/serving/cache.log (sanitized):

```
[02:11:03] route=search-sim tenant=acme req_id=abc123 lookup_key=ctx_v2:sha1:8f3a... pad_seq=256 kernel=attn-fusion-v3 quant=q4_mixed
[02:11:03] route=search-sim tenant=acme req_id=abc123 key_norm=sha1:8f3a... result=MISS
[02:11:03] route=search-sim tenant=acme req_id=abc124 lookup_key=ctx_v1:sha1:8f3a... pad_seq=220 kernel=attn-v2 quant=q8_legacy
[02:11:03] route=search-sim tenant=acme req_id=abc124 result=HIT
```

maria: That looks like key namespace changed from ctx_v1 -> ctx_v2 and pad_seq differs. Could be canonicalization version bump + padding multiplier.

raj: Confirmed: compiler adds padding to match vectorization boundary when attn-fusion enabled. Previously we normalized padding before hashing; new runtime moved padding after keygen. So same logical context gets different key.

alex: Reproducer: run minimal loop against local engine with and without fusion flag; compare cache keys. Command: 

```
./tools/repro_ctx_key --route search-sim --prefix-file samples/prompt.txt --fusion on > keys_with_fusion.txt
./tools/repro_ctx_key --route search-sim --prefix-file samples/prompt.txt --fusion off > keys_without_fusion.txt
diff keys*
```

sophia: Good catch. Does this explain 12% -> 4% for long prompts only?

raj: Yes — longer prompts trigger different pad_seq (multiple of 64) so salt changes. Shorter prompts fall under same pad and keep hits.

maria: Any effect from quantization? q4_mixed may change tokenization preproc ordering?

alex: I checked: quant didn't change keygen directly; it's just a correlated rollout on same pool. Primary culprit is padding+key-version bump. Quant might affect downstream perf but not hit identity.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T01:45:12Z attn-fusion-v3 -> pool-attn-fusion-1 by ci/cd (owner=eng-runtime).

ops-bot: Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/caching-key-regressions (useful for rollback checklist).

maria: Plan: 1) quick hotfix to normalize padding before hash (1h hotfix), 2) long-term: move keygen into canonicalization library so kernel changes can't affect ordering, 3) add unit to guard padding vs hash.

alex: I'm working on PR for the hotfix (will add 2 toggles: COPY -> maintain old keygen behavior; and new canonicalize flag). Will target canary pool first.

raj: Also add metric pfx_cache.key_version and pad_seq distribution to observability so we can alert on sudden shifts.

sophia: Can we roll a targeted rollback of attn-fusion on the 2 affected host pools until fix lands?

alex: Yep, request sent to infra; if rollback takes >30m we'll ship the hotfix as patch to keygen.

maria: Assigning: alex -> hotfix + canary; raj -> metrics and alert; sophia -> rollback coordination; i'll own postmortem and customer comms.

alex: PR link when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
